title: KEEP AN OMER FOR THE GENERATIONS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Moses said, 'This is what the LORD has commanded: "Take an omer of manna and
keep it for the generations to come, so they can see the bread I gave you to eat
in the wilderness when I brought you out of Egypt."' So Moses said to Aaron,
'Take a jar and put an omer of manna in it. Then place it before the LORD to be
kept for the generations to come.'" - Ex 16:32-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God tells them to keep a jar of manna. Not to eat, but to remember.

There is a lovely irony here. Manna kept overnight rotted. Manna kept for
generations, at God's command, endured. The same substance, preserved because God
said so.

The purpose is stated clearly: "so they can see the bread I gave you." Children
not yet born would look at that jar and understand that their ancestors had been
fed by God in a place where nothing grows.

We need our own jars. Not literal ones, necessarily, but ways of preserving
evidence. A note in the margin of a Bible with a date beside it. A journal entry
recording an answered prayer. A story told at the table.

Memory fades faster than we expect. The provision that felt miraculous in March
is barely recalled by September.

Hebrews later mentions this jar, kept in the ark of the covenant (Heb 9:4). God
placed the record of His provision in the most holy place. He wanted it near
Him.

What God has done for you deserves keeping.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God done for you that you have never written down?
2. What would go in your jar?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me to preserve the memory of Your faithfulness so that it is not lost
to me or to those who come after me. Amen.
